name: Migrating from MySQL to MariaDB on CentOS
description:
Migrating from MySQL to MariaDB on CentOS 6

Aims

To provide details for migrating from MySQL 5.1 to MariaDB 10 To provide steps taken for adding repositories for MariaDB To provide steps for installing and migrating MariaDB

Assumptions

  • MySQL 5.1 is installed and running
  • Databases and configuration files for MySQL already exist
  • Upgrade/Migration to latest version of MariaDB (10.0) is required
  • User has some experience with Linux
  • User has root access to the machine
  • User has root access to the MySQL database

Contents

  1. Backup all existing data
  2. Configure Repository for MariaDB 5.5
  3. Remove MySQL
  4. Install MariaDB 5.5
  5. Migrate data to MariaDB
  6. Sanity check
  7. Remove MariaDB 5.5
  8. Reconfigure Repositories
  9. Install MariaDB 10
  10. Migrate data to new version
  11. Update configuration files

name: Backup existing data
description:
Notes

MariaDB is a drop-in replacement for MySQL, ie the service is still called 'mysqld' and you will not need to change any code to access the database. You will need to stop the MySQL server while you perform the migration. While the migration is running the database will not be accessible. You can always tell whether you are running MySQL or MariaDB with the command

mysql --version

1. Backup existing data

Make sure you backup all DATA and CONFIGURATION files in case you experience failure while migrating/updating data.

1.1 Backup data using mysql_dump:

[root@centos tmp]# mysqldump -u root -p --all-databases > /tmp/mysql_backup.sql
Enter password: 
-- Warning: Skipping the data of table mysql.event. Specify the --events option explicitly.
[root@centos tmp]# ll mysql_backup.sql 
-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 3921927 Apr  3 15:30 mysql_backup.sql
[root@centos tmp]#

1.2 Copy the MySQL configuration file to the /tmp folder as well

[root@centos tmp]# cp /etc/my.cnf /tmp/
[root@centos tmp]#

1.3 Stop the MySQL server

[root@centos tmp]# service mysqld stop
Stopping mysqld:                                           [  OK  ]
[root@centos tmp]#

1.4 Backup the MySQL DATA directory as well for in case:

[root@centos tmp]# cp -R /var/lib/mysql /tmp/mysql_datadir
[root@centos tmp]#

You now have the SQL Schema and table backed up to /tmp/mysql_backup.sql You now have the MySQL config files backed up to /tmp/my.cnf You now have the MySQL DATA folder backed up to /tmp/mysql_datadir/

name: Configure Repository for MariaDB
description:
2. Configure Repository for MariaDB 5.5

Get the correct repository details from https://downloads.mariadb.org/mariadb/repositories/#mirror=nixnet&distro=CentOS&distro_release=centos6-amd64--centos6&version=5.5

You can copy and paste the contents into a new file:

# MariaDB 5.5 CentOS repository list - created 2015-04-03 12:03 UTC
# http://mariadb.org/mariadb/repositories/
[mariadb]
name = MariaDB
baseurl = http://yum.mariadb.org/5.5/centos6-amd64
gpgkey=https://yum.mariadb.org/RPM-GPG-KEY-MariaDB
gpgcheck=1

or run this command:

[root@centos tmp]# echo "# MariaDB 5.5 CentOS repository list - created 2015-04-03 12:03 UTC
> # http://mariadb.org/mariadb/repositories/
> [mariadb]
> name = MariaDB
> baseurl = http://yum.mariadb.org/5.5/centos6-amd64
> gpgkey=https://yum.mariadb.org/RPM-GPG-KEY-MariaDB
> gpgcheck=1" > /etc/yum.repos.d/mariadb55.repo

This will create a new repository file called /etc/yum.repos.d/mariadb55.repo

NOTE: You must upgrade to v5.5 first. Upgrading directly to version 10.0 will fail.

Clean the yum cache:

[root@centos tmp]# yum clean all
Loaded plugins: fastestmirror, refresh-packagekit, security
Cleaning repos: base epel extras mariadb mongodb-org-3.0 updates
Cleaning up Everything
Cleaning up list of fastest mirrors
[root@centos tmp]#

Note that 'mariadb' is now in the list of repos. If it is not, check that /etc/yum.repos.d/mariadb55.repo exists and has the correct content.

name: Install MariaDB
description:
4. Install MariaDB 5.5

You can now install the new MariaDB server. NOTE The commands are exactly the same as installing MySQL. Remember that MariaDB uses the same names (including package names) as MySQL.

Check that yum will install MariaDB-Galera-server before you confirm:

[root@centos tmp]# service mysql start

[root@centos tmp]#

name: Migrate data to MariaDB
description:
5. Migrate data to MariaDB

To migrate the data, all you need to do is run the 'mysql-upgrade' command. MariaDB will migrate the data in your database. You should not need to restore anything from the database.

The 'mysql' service must be running for this command. Authenticate if necessary (the mysql passwords will all be the same as before the upgrade):

name: Sanity check
description:
6. Sanity check

Run 'mysql' from the command line and check that all the databases are in place:

[root@centos tmp]# mysql -u root -p

If you see all your databases, everything should be fine. You can now upgrade to MariaDB 10

name: Remove MariaDB
description:
7. Remove MariaDB 5.5

Remove the MariaDB server and client packages:

[root@centos tmp]# yum remove mysql-server mysql-client

name: Reconfigure Repositories
description:
8. Reconfigure Repositories

You will need to add the repository for MariaDB 10, and remove the repository for MariaDB 5.5

8.1 Disable the MariaDB 5.5 repository This assumes you created the repository file in /etc/yum.repos.d/mariadb55.repo as detailed in Step 2:

[root@centos tmp]# mv /etc/yum.repos.d/mariadb55.repo /etc/yum.repos.d/mariadb55.repo.disabled
[root@centos tmp]#

8.2 Add the MariaDB 10 repository Get the correct repository details from https://downloads.mariadb.org/mariadb/repositories/#mirror=nixnet&distro=CentOS&distro_release=centos6-amd64--centos6&version=10.0

You can copy and paste the contents into a new file:

# MariaDB 10.0 CentOS repository list - created 2015-04-03 13:06 UTC
# http://mariadb.org/mariadb/repositories/
[mariadb]
name = MariaDB
baseurl = http://yum.mariadb.org/10.0/centos6-amd64
gpgkey=https://yum.mariadb.org/RPM-GPG-KEY-MariaDB
gpgcheck=1

or run this command:

[root@centos tmp]# echo "# MariaDB 10.0 CentOS repository list - created 2015-04-03 13:06 UTC
> # http://mariadb.org/mariadb/repositories/
> [mariadb]
> name = MariaDB
> baseurl = http://yum.mariadb.org/10.0/centos6-amd64
> gpgkey=https://yum.mariadb.org/RPM-GPG-KEY-MariaDB
> gpgcheck=1" > /etc/yum.repos.d/mariadb10.repo
[root@centos tmp]#

This will create a new repository file called /etc/yum.repos.d/mariadb10.repo

8.3 Clean the yum cache as before:

[root@centos tmp]# yum clean all
Loaded plugins: fastestmirror, refresh-packagekit, security
Cleaning repos: base epel extras mariadb mongodb-org-3.0 updates
Cleaning up Everything
Cleaning up list of fastest mirrors
[root@centos tmp]#

  1. Update configuration files

MariaDB configuration files are split up and stored in the folder /etc/my.cnf.d/

You will need to copy and paste any configurations that you have made to the original MySQL installation to the correct places in the MariaDB files.

For example:

[root@centos tmp]# cat my.cnf 
[mysqld]
datadir=/var/lib/mysql
socket=/var/lib/mysql/mysql.sock
user=mysql
# Disabling symbolic-links is recommended to prevent assorted security risks
symbolic-links=0

[mysqld_safe]
log-error=/var/log/mysqld.log
pid-file=/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.pid

The [mysqld] section exists in /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf:

[root@centos tmp]# cat /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf 
#
# These groups are read by MariaDB server.
# Use it for options that only the server (but not clients) should see
#
# See the examples of server my.cnf files in /usr/share/mysql/
#

# this is read by the standalone daemon and embedded servers
[server]

# this is only for the mysqld standalone daemon
[mysqld]

# this is only for embedded server
[embedded]

# This group is only read by MariaDB servers, not by MySQL.
# If you use the same .cnf file for MySQL and MariaDB,
# you can put MariaDB-only options here
[mariadb]

# This group is only read by MariaDB-10.0 servers.
# If you use the same .cnf file for MariaDB of different versions,
# use this group for options that older servers don't understand
[mariadb-10.0]

[root@centos tmp]#

Copy and paste the options for the [mysqld] section into the new file, so that it looks like this:

[root@centos tmp]# cat /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf 
#
# These groups are read by MariaDB server.
# Use it for options that only the server (but not clients) should see
#
# See the examples of server my.cnf files in /usr/share/mysql/
#

# this is read by the standalone daemon and embedded servers
[server]

# this is only for the mysqld standalone daemon
[mysqld]
datadir=/var/lib/mysql
socket=/var/lib/mysql/mysql.sock
user=mysql
# Disabling symbolic-links is recommended to prevent assorted security risks
symbolic-links=0

[mysqld_safe]
log-error=/var/log/mysqld.log
pid-file=/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.pid

# this is only for embedded server
[embedded]

# This group is only read by MariaDB servers, not by MySQL.
# If you use the same .cnf file for MySQL and MariaDB,
# you can put MariaDB-only options here
[mariadb]

# This group is only read by MariaDB-10.0 servers.
# If you use the same .cnf file for MariaDB of different versions,
# use this group for options that older servers don't understand
[mariadb-10.0]

[root@centos tmp]#

Restart the mysql service to load the new changes:

[root@centos tmp]# service mysql restart
Shutting down MySQL...                                     [  OK  ]
Starting MySQL.                                            [  OK  ]
[root@centos tmp]#

MariaDB 10 is now installed and ready for use.
